presentingComplaint: Progressive ascending limb weakness and tingling over 6 days
history: 6-day history of symmetrical weakness beginning in both feet and ascending to the thighs, now involving the hands, with distal paraesthesiae. Difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair; two falls at home. Reports an episode of watery diarrhoea about 2 weeks earlier that resolved spontaneously (possible Campylobacter). No fever currently, no bladder or bowel dysfunction, no back pain, no sensory level. Denies preceding trauma or new drugs. No significant PMH; not diabetic; no alcohol excess.
examination: Symmetrical flaccid weakness, MRC grade 3/5 lower limbs and 4/5 upper limbs, distal more than proximal. Areflexia - knee and ankle jerks absent, upper-limb reflexes absent. Plantars flexor. Mild glove-and-stocking reduction in pinprick with preserved joint position sense; no sensory level. Cranial nerves intact, no ophthalmoplegia; bilateral facial weakness absent at present. No neck stiffness. Single-breath count 22; forced vital capacity 1.9 L (declining). No bladder distension.
imaging: MRI whole spine with contrast: normal cord, no compressive lesion; may show enhancement of anterior nerve roots / cauda equina supporting GBS. MRI performed principally to exclude cord compression.
microbiology: Stool culture negative at presentation; Campylobacter jejuni serology pending. n/a for empiric antimicrobials.
finalDiagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP)
citations: Harrison 22e - Guillain-Barré Syndrome and Other Immune-Mediated Neuropathies
AAN Guideline: Intravenous Immunoglobulin in the Treatment of Guillain-Barré Syndrome 2012
stewardship: not applicable - non-infective. GBS is a post-infectious autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy; treatment is IVIG 2 g/kg over 5 days or plasma exchange, not antibiotics.
contraindications: IVIG: caution in IgA deficiency (anaphylaxis risk), thrombotic events, and renal impairment (osmotic nephrosis) - hydrate and check IgA/renal function
Corticosteroids are NOT effective in GBS and should be avoided as monotherapy
edgeCases: Miller Fisher variant (ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia, anti-GQ1b positive) presents without limb weakness
Autonomic dysfunction (labile BP, arrhythmia) can be life-threatening; do NOT be reassured by an isolated tachycardia/hypertension
Early CSF protein may be normal in the first week - normal protein does not exclude GBS
expectedMaiK: Ascending symmetrical flaccid weakness with areflesia and CSF albuminocytological dissociation after a diarrhoeal illness is classic Guillain-Barré syndrome; the priority is serial respiratory monitoring (FVC/single-breath count) because neuromuscular respiratory failure can develop rapidly and may need intubation before hypoxia appears.
expectedNextQuestions: Any preceding respiratory or diarrhoeal infection in the last 4 weeks?
Is there any breathing difficulty, difficulty swallowing, or double vision?
Is the weakness ascending and symmetrical, and are there any bladder/bowel or sensory-level symptoms?
expectedInvestigations: Serial bedside spirometry (FVC) and single-breath count for respiratory monitoring
